genZNote: The organism behind bread, beer, and half of molecular biology. If a eukaryotic genetics experiment exists, there's a good chance this yeast did it first.

morphology.arrangement: Single cells or budding pairs/short chains
morphology.oxygenRequirement: Facultative anaerobe (ferments in low O2, respires aerobically)
morphology.notes: Reproduces primarily by multilateral budding; can also form ascospores under nutrient-limited conditions.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Fruit skins, plant surfaces, soil, and fermenting sugary substrates
habitat.hostAssociation: Not part of normal human microbiota; occasionally an opportunistic pathogen in severely immunocompromised patients or from probiotic overuse
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Ubiquitous on ripe fruit and in wineries, bakeries, and breweries; the classic domesticated fermentation organism

microscopy.appearance: Oval budding yeast cells, no true hyphae under normal growth

culture.growthCharacteristics: Rapid growth at 25-30°C; ferments glucose to ethanol and CO2 under anaerobic conditions
culture.colonyMorphology: Smooth, creamy white to tan, dome-shaped colonies

identificationClues: Oval budding cells with no true hyphae distinguish it from molds and from Candida's pseudohyphae
Vigorous fermentation of glucose (CO2 production) is the classic bread/beer/wine signature
Grows well on simple media at 25-30°C; not a fastidious organism
Germ tube negative — helps rule out Candida albicans if morphology is ambiguous

diseases: Rare opportunistic fungemia in severely immunocompromised or ICU patients, sometimes linked to probiotic supplement use
clinicalImportance.transmission: Not typically transmitted person-to-person; rare infections arise from ingestion of probiotic supplements or catheter contamination
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Overwhelmingly a beneficial/industrial organism; clinical disease is a rare exception, not the rule
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Distinguishing from Candida species matters in the rare clinical isolate, since S. cerevisiae behaves very differently in susceptibility and significance

examFacts.importantDisease: Rare opportunistic fungemia (exception, not the rule)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: The classic fermentation yeast of bread, beer, and wine; also the foundational eukaryotic model organism in genetics
